original_question: Let P be a family of at least two essentially distinct integer polynomials, and let dmin(P) be the least d such that the Host–Kra factor Zd,T is characteristic for mean convergence of the averages (1/N) Σ T^{p1(n)} f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)} fℓ. Must one always have dmin(P) ≤ |P| - 1?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1 (Powers of a single transformation), specifically the open problem stated as Problem 8 in the 2016 arXiv version: for a family P of essentially distinct integer polynomials, prove that dmin(P) ≤ |P|−1. This is the exact statement your draft is aiming at. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target almost verbatim: it uses a family P of at least two essentially distinct integer polynomials, the minimal Host–Kra level dmin(P), the characteristic-factor interpretation via Z_{d,T}, and the precise bound dmin(P) ≤ |P|−1 that the paper asks about. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: P should be specified explicitly as P = {p1, ..., pℓ} ⊂ ℤ[n], i.e. a family of one-variable integer polynomials with ℓ = |P| ≥ 2. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The ambient dynamical setting should be stated: (X, 𝓧, μ, T) is an invertible measure-preserving system. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
The functions should be quantified as f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(μ). ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Essentially distinct should be unpacked as: every p_i is nonconstant and every difference p_i − p_j for i ≠ j is nonconstant. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

dmin(P) should be defined uniformly over all such systems and all such bounded tuples of functions: it is the minimal d for which the preceding theorem works, and d depends only on P, not on the system or the functions. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To make the question fully stand-alone, mean convergence should be identified as L^2(μ)-convergence, which is the paper’s ambient notion of mean convergence/characteristic factors. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

A paper-faithful formulation should avoid switching to the neighboring Weyl-system quantity dW_min(P) or to the separate adjacent problem dmin(P) = dW_min(P); those are distinct questions in the paper. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~nikosf/OpenProblems/Polynomial.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let P = {p1, ..., pℓ} ⊂ ℤ[n] be a family of one-variable integer polynomials with ℓ ≥ 2 such that each p_i and each difference p_i − p_j for i ≠ j is nonconstant. For each invertible measure-preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and each f1, ..., fℓ ∈ L∞(μ), consider the polynomial multiple ergodic averages A_N = (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)}fℓ. Let dmin(P) be the least integer d such that, for every such system and every such choice of functions, the Host–Kra factor Z_{d,T} is characteristic for the L^2(μ)-mean convergence of A_N. Is it always true that dmin(P) ≤ ℓ − 1 = |P| − 1? ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because the paper first states the theorem that some finite Host–Kra factor Z_{d,T} is characteristic for these polynomial averages, then defines dmin(P), and then poses exactly the bound dmin(P) ≤ |P|−1 as the open problem. The nearby Weyl-system bound for dW_min(P) is presented only as a special case, and the equality dmin(P) = dW_min(P) is posed separately as the next problem, so replacing your draft by either of those would shift away from the paper’s actual target. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
